newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Italian soldiers learn Albanian for "Drop the gun".
newsitem.headline: Italian soldiers learn Albanian for "Drop the gun".

text.p: Italian soldiers heading for Albania are being given a specially prepared guide to the violence-ridden country that includes handy Albanian phrases such as "Drop the gun!"

Italian officials in Albania said the booklet was designed to help the 2,500 Italian soldiers prepare for their mission to the country that has been hit by weeks of near anarchy after popular investment schemes failed and jilted savers revolted.
Aside from that most useful phrase -- "Hidhni armet!" (Drop the gun!) -- the booklet also includes phrases such as "Mirmengjes" (Good day!) and "Ndal" (Stop!)
"It is a very handy booklet," said one Italian official in Tirana. "It gives them the words they need in Albania, the normal sort of things they may need to say."

The booklet also offers the Italian soldiers, who will be leading the 6,000-strong force due to begin arriving here within days to protect emergency food and medicine supplies, helpful tips on Albanian culture.
Albanians, for example, will become quickly annoyed at anyone who yell insults at women, the guide says.
It also urges the soldiers to avoid conversations with local residents about religion because Albanians can react angrily.

More than 200 people have been killed and about 700 injured since the uprising began earlier this year when get-rich-quick pyramid investment schemes failed and armed rebels took control of the south during unchecked looting and banditry.
Army arsenals were looted after soldiers and police abandoned their posts while automatic rifles and weapons were seized by citizens who brandished them on the streets.
